blocks.text: The endpoint that creates a document has no working rate limit. The check is in the code, but production does not turn it on. At 200 requests per second, one client uses up the free daily database writes in about four minutes. I recommend the Cloudflare rate limiter, which costs nothing per request. Confirm it in the decisions at the end.

decisions.q: Which rate limiter should we put in front of POST /api/session?
decisions.why: The Cloudflare limiter costs nothing to run and stops the abuse we saw. The KV counter is better only if we need a limit for each user, and the roadmap has no such need.

opts.label: Cloudflare Rate Limiting binding
opts.detail: It takes hours to ship and has no storage cost. It cannot set a limit for each user.

opts.label: Custom KV counter
opts.detail: It can set a limit for each user. It costs one KV write per request, and a short burst can get through.

decisions.q: How should the limit reach production?
decisions.why: Start in shadow mode, because it costs little and shows the effect on real traffic. You can take the other two options in any combination.

opts.label: Shadow mode for one week
opts.detail: Log each request that the limit would stop. Do not stop any request.

opts.label: Alert on sustained 429s
opts.detail: If a real client hits the limit, the limit is too low.

opts.label: Raise the limit to 30 per minute
opts.detail: An agent that publishes several documents in one run can need more than 10 per minute.

glossary.def: The most requests one client can send in a time window. The API rejects the rest with a 429 error.
